dedupe_keys.name: crtc national public alerting system implementation summary canada

description: This CRTC dataset summarises how Canadian last-mile distributors take part in the National Public Alerting System (NPAS), the system behind Alert Ready emergency alerts. The CRTC requires wireless service providers, cable, satellite and IP television providers, and radio and television broadcasters, collectively called last-mile distributors, to distribute emergency alerts issued by authorities, and it enforces these rules. The dataset reports distributors' participation in the alerting system as a criterion of the industry's annual compliance, together with the number of staff investigations opened to resolve NPAS compliance matters. It was first published in March 2025 and updated in August 2026. Coverage: Canada. Format and access: CSV and XLSX data with a PDF data dictionary, in English and French, free under the Open Government Licence - Canada. Caveats: a compliance summary, not a log of alerts sent or of their delivery times; the level of detail by distributor type was not checked. Simulation uses: parameters for emergency warning reach through broadcast and mobile channels, and context for studies of alerting when telecom networks fail. Related records: the US nationwide alert test case study and the Hawaii false missile alert case describe alerting performance, and the Rogers outage review shows loss of alerting and 911 during an outage.
name: CRTC National Public Alerting System implementation summary (Canada)
